script.name: Lipoprotein metabolism
script.purpose: Carries triglycerides and cholesterol, which do not dissolve in water, through the blood in lipoproteins: from the gut (the exogenous pathway), from the liver (the endogenous pathway) and back to the liver (reverse cholesterol transport).
steps: the intestine packages dietary fat into chylomicrons, which carry apoB-48
lipoprotein lipase in capillaries releases fatty acids from chylomicrons and VLDL
the liver takes up chylomicron remnants through apoE
the liver secretes VLDL, which carries apoB-100 and becomes IDL and then LDL
LDL delivers cholesterol to tissues through LDL receptors, which bind apoB-100
HDL collects cholesterol from tissues and returns it to the liver (reverse cholesterol transport)
regulation: LCAT, activated by apoA-I, esterifies cholesterol in HDL
cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) moves cholesteryl esters from HDL to VLDL and LDL
cofactors: apoB-100 for binding the LDL receptor
deficiencies: familial chylomicronemia (type I): lipoprotein lipase or apoC-II deficiency, with very high triglycerides, pancreatitis and eruptive xanthomas
familial hypercholesterolemia (type IIa): a defective LDL receptor, with very high LDL, tendon xanthomas and early heart attacks
dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III): apoE2 variant, with palmar xanthomas
abetalipoproteinemia: MTP deficiency, with no apoB lipoproteins, fat malabsorption, acanthocytes and vitamin E deficiency
drug_targets: statins raise the number of LDL receptors
PCSK9 inhibitors stop LDL receptors from being broken down
fibrates activate PPAR-alpha and lipoprotein lipase, lowering triglycerides
ezetimibe blocks cholesterol absorption in the intestine
treatment: familial hypercholesterolemia: high-intensity statin, then ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors
familial chylomicronemia: a very low-fat diet
abetalipoproteinemia: fat-soluble vitamins, especially vitamin E, and a low-fat diet
pearls: Chylomicrons carry apoB-48; VLDL, IDL and LDL carry apoB-100.
Triglycerides above 1000 mg/dL make the plasma milky and raise the risk of acute pancreatitis.
Tendon xanthomas, especially of the Achilles tendon, suggest familial hypercholesterolemia.

sources.title: 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
